title: Visual Stimulus Discrimination in Danionella cerebrum and Danio rerio
author: Zanon, Potrich, et al.
materials: Flexible white corrugated polypropylene sheet (3.5 mm thickness)
Aquarium Amtra Wave Zen Artist 40L tank

steps.title: Obtain ethical approval
steps.instruction: Secure written approval from your institution’s animal care committee covering housing conditions, isolation duration, and the behavioral testing setup.

steps.title: Prepare stimulus presentation system
steps.instruction: Set up the visual stimulus cards, verify that stimulus size, contrast and visibility match the species, and calculate the visual angle using α = arctan(l / 2d) where l is the smallest element dimension and d is the maximum viewing distance (20 cm). Ensure the resulting visual angle exceeds the species’ discrimination threshold.

steps.title: Prepare recording system
steps.instruction: Install the monitoring camera or other tracking device, adjust frame rate and focus to obtain continuous, glare‑free video of individual fish throughout the trial.

steps.title: Assemble experimental corridors
steps.instruction: Place the experimental corridors inside the testing tank, scaling dimensions to the species size (e.g., 7 × 20 × 0.4 cm polypropylene strips). Multiple corridors may be installed in parallel to increase throughput.

steps.title: Condition testing room
steps.instruction: Arrange the behavioral testing room to keep ambient noise low and maintain stable illumination and temperature throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Design visual stimuli
steps.instruction: Create square‑arena stimuli (6 × 6 cm) containing dot arrays for the numerosity task. Control total dot area, perimeter, dot radius, inter‑dot distance and convex hull across habituation trials; keep numerosity constant during habituation and change it only for the single dishabituation trial.

steps.title: Generate stimulus images
steps.instruction: Use MATLAB with the GeNEsIS software to generate the dot‑array images and save each as a .png file.

steps.title: Print stimuli on heavy paper
steps.instruction: Print each .png stimulus on 160 g/m² paper to ensure flatness during later lamination.

steps.title: Laminate and cut stimuli
steps.instruction: Laminate the printed sheets, then cut them precisely so that laminate edges are fully sealed and free of gaps (preventing water ingress).

steps.title: Mount stimuli to strips
steps.instruction: Attach each laminated 6 × 6 cm stimulus to the lower portion of a 7 × 20 × 0.4 cm polypropylene strip using a water‑resistant adhesive, then verify that the mounted stimulus fits snugly into the corridor short side without insertion problems and remains fully submerged (water depth = 7 cm).

steps.title: Record behavioral trials
steps.instruction: Place a single fish in a corridor, start video recording for a 20‑minute trial, and ensure continuous tracking of the fish’s position throughout.

steps.title: Define stimulus zone
steps.instruction: Consider the fish “close to the stimulus” when it is within the first 15 % of the corridor length (3 cm of a 20 cm corridor), corresponding to roughly two average body lengths for Danionella.

steps.title: Score fish position
steps.instruction: Either manually time how long the fish stays in the stimulus zone or use a tracking tool such as DeepLabCut to label and track the fish head, extracting the time spent in the zone for the first 180 seconds of each trial.

steps.title: Calculate proportion near stimulus
steps.instruction: Compute proportion = (seconds spent in stimulus zone) / 180 for each trial.

steps.title: Compute daily differential score
steps.instruction: For each day, calculate Differential score = (proportion in Trial 6) – (mean proportion of Trials 1–5).

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Across the five days, test habituation by comparing the Day 4 differential score to zero with a Wilcoxon signed‑rank test or one‑sample t‑test. Test dishabituation by comparing Day 4 versus Day 5 differential scores using a permutation ANOVA (e.g., aovperm in the permuco R package, 5000 permutations) with Control Type as a factor.

steps.title: Apply exclusion criteria
steps.instruction: Exclude any fish that remains immobile for >50 % of the analyzed 180 s, shows signs of distress, or for which tracking fails (typically <5 % of trials).
